summary:
Backend-only verification of iter19 parlay diversity tightening (max_same_sport_for_target) + frontend lint of parlay.tsx unification. 13/13 backend tests PASS. ESLint clean (0 errors, 1 acceptable 'Pick' unused-var warning).

— Feature 5 (cap math): all 5 sanity points verified — target=5→2, 8→3, 10→4, 15→5, 20→6. Also 2-3 legs → 2.
— Feature 1 (high-risk 72h diversity): cap is enforced against requested target_legs (10) → 4. All 3 parlays respect cap=4 (top sport = 4 in each). All 3 parlays have ≥2 distinct sports (Soccer + MLB).
— Feature 2 (high-risk structure): exactly 3 parlays returned, labels = {SAFE, BALANCED, AGGRESSIVE}, each has 8 legs (≥5 required).
— Feature 3 (standard 24h): 3 parlays returned, each ≥2 legs.
— Feature 4 (lint): `npx eslint app/(tabs)/parlay.tsx` → 0 errors, 1 warning (`'Pick' is defined but never used`).
— Frontend confirmation: `isCustomWithIncludes` helper defined at parlay.tsx:47 as documented; chip-row render at line ~290 unified across AUTO/CUSTOM/SINGLE.

OBSERVATION (not a regression — diagnostic): With current 72h pool (74 Soccer / 19 MLB / 2 Tennis), the optimizer stops at 8 legs (not 10) and the post-truncation Soccer share is 50% (4 of 8) in every parlay. The 40% cap is correctly applied against target_legs=10 (=4) — but because the parlay truncates to 8 legs the *observed* ratio is 50%. Tennis (only 2 picks in 72h) cannot reliably contribute a 3rd sport leg. This matches the main-agent's predicted distribution (~4 Soccer / 2-4 MLB / 0-2 Tennis).

minor.issue: Top-sport ratio of FINAL delivered parlay is 50% (4 Soccer of 8 legs) because the optimizer truncates from 10→8 legs while the same-sport cap was computed against the original target of 10. User-perceived 'mostly Soccer' feeling may persist on 8-leg deliveries even though the cap math is technically respected. Consider re-applying the cap against actual leg count post-build, OR boosting Tennis/UFC inventory in the 72h pool. With current slate this is the practical ceiling.

action_items: OPTIONAL — Apply max_same_sport_for_target against the *current* leg count after build completes, not only against the original target. Would deliver ≤40% in the final parlay regardless of early truncation. Today cap=4 is enforced vs target=10, but final delivered parlay has 8 legs → 50% Soccer.

OPTIONAL — Backend could broaden the 72h pool (e.g. relax Tennis eligibility to lock≥70 in high-risk mode) so a 3rd sport can actually enter the parlay; right now only 2 Tennis picks in 72h means no Tennis legs survive damage-control + diversification.
Cosmetic — remove the unused `Pick` import at /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/parlay.tsx:10 to clear the lone eslint warning.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/backend/parlay_optimizer.py:65-71 — max_same_sport_for_target correctly tightened: 2-5→2, 6-10→floor(target*4/10), 11-20→floor(target/3). All 5 spec points verified.

/app/backend/parlay_optimizer.py:418-460 — diversification_ok uses target_legs (not len(legs)) for the same-sport cap. This is the source of the 50% post-truncation observation: when build stops at 8 of 10 legs, 4 same-sport legs (40% of 10) are 50% of 8. Not a bug per se — just a UX artefact worth flagging.
/app/frontend/app/(tabs)/parlay.tsx:47-50 — isCustomWithIncludes helper present, signature matches spec (mode + included[] → bool).

/app/frontend/app/(tabs)/parlay.tsx:290-360 — sport chip row now always rendered; chipActive logic correctly branches on isAuto/isCustom/isSingle. AUTO chips read-only (all active), CUSTOM uses includeChip styling for multi-select, SINGLE is single-select. Matches PR description.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_parlay_diversity_iter19.py (NEW — 13 tests: 6 cap-math unit tests + 1 standard 24h + 6 high-risk 72h including diversity, structure, and post-truncation diagnostic)

If the live slate shifts and the optimizer starts producing 10-leg parlays (vs current 8), the test_post_truncation_sport_ratio_observation diagnostic line will print actual ratios — the 60% ceiling there still holds. The target-based cap test (test_sport_diversity_within_implementation_cap) is the load-bearing diversity check; it's pegged to max_same_sport_for_target(10) = 4.
rca_of_issue: n/a — verification run, no failures found. The original 'all soccer' complaint is structurally addressed at the cap layer (40% of 6-10 legs, 33% of 11-20). The only remaining UX exposure is the post-truncation ratio: a build that target=10 but stops at 8 legs can deliver 50% same-sport even though the cap of 4 is technically respected. Recommend the optional re-apply-on-actual-length fix above if main agent wants the user-visible ratio to also be ≤40%.
